summary: Feed s123_double is degraded for NDR: 100% of frames are VXLAN-encapsulated and 97.3% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 90%). NDR sees only outer tunnel headers and ciphertext, severely limiting detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic without stripping. All 3177/3177 frames arrive inside VXLAN (100% vs 10% threshold), so the NDR only sees outer VTEP headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot parse inner L2-L7 headers, flow 5-tuple, or payload. Correlation, IDS signatures, and behavioral detection fail on encapsulated traffic - effectively blind to 100% of inner flows.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN at the packet broker to present inner Ethernet/IP frames to the NDR so it can parse flows and apply detection. Preserve VNI as metadata/tag if needed for tenant context.

findings.root_cause: 97.26% of bytes are encrypted vs NDR tolerance of 90%. Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted with no decryption or key-sharing before the tool, leaving only headers visible.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection and threat detection. With 97% ciphertext, payload analysis, JA3, file extraction, and C2 detection are blind, reducing detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt selected TLS at packet broker / forward session keys to NDR, or filter to send only decryptable/policy-relevant encrypted flows to NDR to bring encrypted share below 90% and restore payload visibility.
